result.title: Refuse: inappropriate development, no very special circumstances

findings.text: The land is grey belt: it does not strongly contribute to purposes (a), (b) or (d).
Uses grey belt land and would not fundamentally undermine the remaining Green Belt.
There is an evidenced unmet need for housing (footnote 41).
Evidence gap: the Connectivity Tool has not been run, although TR3(2) says it "should be used alongside other relevant quantitative or qualitative evidence".
Not a sustainable location with reference to TR3: the location does not offer a genuine choice of transport modes, so GB7(1)(g) is not met.
Does not comply with the Golden Rules (GB8).
In a location known to be at risk of flooding, F7(2)(a) to (e) are not demonstrated, so the proposal "should be refused".
An unacceptable impact on highway safety: the proposal "should be refused" (TR6(4)).
Conflicts with DP3(1) or (2), or with explicit local design standards, without clear justification: DP3(3) says it "should be refused".
Harm to landscape character and the character of the area, given limited weight.
Conflict with development plan policies, given limited weight.
New homes towards evidenced needs attract substantial weight (HO7(1)).
Short-term economic benefits of construction and occupation.
Inappropriate development in the Green Belt, to be approved only in very special circumstances (GB6).
Harm to the Green Belt by reason of inappropriateness, and to its openness, carries substantial weight (GB6(2)).

pdl.title: Previously developed land route, GB7(1)(e), on the applicant's case

result.title: Refuse: fails a policy that says development "should be refused"

findings.text: Redevelopment of previously developed land without substantial harm to openness, so it is not inappropriate development.
Evidence gap: the Connectivity Tool has not been run, although TR3(2) says it "should be used alongside other relevant quantitative or qualitative evidence".
The location would not limit the need to travel by private car or offer a genuine choice of transport modes (TR3(1)(a)).
In a location known to be at risk of flooding, F7(2)(a) to (e) are not demonstrated, so the proposal "should be refused".
An unacceptable impact on highway safety: the proposal "should be refused" (TR6(4)).
Conflicts with DP3(1) or (2), or with explicit local design standards, without clear justification: DP3(3) says it "should be refused".
Harm to landscape character and the character of the area, given limited weight.
Conflict with development plan policies, given limited weight.
New homes towards evidenced needs attract substantial weight (HO7(1)).
Short-term economic benefits of construction and occupation.
Not inappropriate development in the Green Belt: approve unless the benefits are substantially outweighed (S5(5)).
